raw_recipe.headline: Candied Kielbasa
raw_recipe.description: Slow cooking brings out the spicy sweetness of this Kielbasa dish--made zesty with ketchup, horseradish, and brown sugar.
raw_recipe.name: Candied Kielbasa

recipeInstructions.text: In a slow cooker combine the sugar, ketchup and horseradish. Add the sausage, and mix well. Cook on High until it starts to boil. Reduce heat to Low, and cook until sauce thickens, about 45 minutes to 1 hour.

review.reviewBody: This is one of our favorites! I have found through trial and error, it is better baked in the oven rather than the slow cooker. Oven cooking gives it more of a "candied" apperarance, whereas the crock-pot version is more watery. If you want to try it the oven way, just well-grease a 13 X 9 dish and bake at 350 for 90 minutes, stirring after every 30 minutes (or until it's as done as your family likes it. My husband prefers it a little dark.) Don't be afraid to try this recipe; it's really easy and nearly everyone who tastes it, just loves it! Good Luck!

This is absolutely fantastic!!!! I read almost every review and here's what I did, I doubled the sauce recipe, fried my kielbasa first for color and then I added 3 sweet peppers (2 red and 1 yellow) and onions in big chunks then put the sauce over the top and put the whole skillet in the oven for 45 min at 350*, and left it do its thing. I served it with homemade Mac and cheese and creamed cucumbers and homemade rolls!!!! my husband had 3 servings and since I had so much sauce, he was eating the sauce on everything, even dipping his rolls into the sauce, lol. I had leftovers, so the next day we was eating the sauce on pulled pork sandwiches. the sauce is the bomb!!! Wish I could give this 10 stars

Yum! Based on other reviewers, I reduced the brown sugar to 2/3rd cup and probably could have reduced to 1/2 cup. Doubled the sauce (used 1/2 cup ketchup and 1/2 cup Sweet Baby Ray BBQ sauce and probably 1 TBSP of Worcestershire). Cut up 2 medium sweet onions and 2 peppers (large chunks 1-2 inches). Placed all in a 9 x 13 pan and baked at 350 for 90 minutes (stirring every 30). Served over rice. Gets even better as it sits. Could have made it on the stove. Next time, will consider reducing brown sugar even more and might consider adding some pineapple chunks near the end. Will certainly make again!

It was a great recipe to make. My children, who eat all of nothing, loved it, as wel as my husband. I did use half the ketchup, substituting the remaining amount with spicy honey BBQ sauce. It was delicious. I also added orange and yellow bell peppers. I cooked it in the oven for for 90 minutes as suggested by another person here, then I put the over on broil for 10 minutes, allowing it to get more of a candied look, also recommended by another person here. It was delicious! I will be making it again.

Wow ~ Delish!
I was looking for something easy for dinner and went to my old stand by of kielbasa but wanted to try something a little different. When I found this recipe, I thought my picky husband might like it because of the horseradish so I gave it a try. I followed sone others suggestions and used 1/4 c. barbeque sauce, 1/4 c. ketchup, 1/2 c. brown sugar, 1/4 c. horseradish, 2 tsp Dijon mustard abd 2 splashes Worcestershire sauce. Instead of the crockpot, I used my oven, 90 minutes @ 350°. Every 30 minutes I would baste the kielbasa with the sauce. I had sides of roasted butternut squash and buttered egg noodles. Absolutely delicious dinner. The husband ate it up like he was starving. I'll keep this recipe around for future use.

This recipe was out of this world! Delicious!

The changes I made: cutting the brown sugar down from 1 cup to 3/4 cup. Also, added 1 chopped white onion and mixed it in with the sausage and ingredients.

Baked it in the oven for 90 minutes at 350 degrees. Stirred every 30 minutes.

It caramelized very nicely and the flavor was perfect. Will make this one over and over again. Thanks for the recipe!

This is fantastic. I used turkey kielbasa and made it on the stovetop in a pan so that I could reduce the sauce. It was very watery at first, but 30 minutes of careful simmering fixed it down into a deep dark beautiful homemade barbecue-sauce coating my kielbasa. Served on slider buns with fresh pineapple and spinach salad. Thanks for sharing!

I make this in the oven, uncovered at 350 degrees for about 45-50 minutes, and then I broil it for 10 minutes. The sauce thickens nicely and the sausage browns on the edges. I do stir pretty often, just so that it cooks evenly. I also add chopped onions and green peppers - the whole family loves it! I typically make it with cheesy potatoes.

Much prefer it as appetizer. Slice kielbasy into bite size pieces and cover with 1/2 cup molasses. Broil for 5 to 8 minutes (little char adds wonders) and turn to broil 3-5 minutes longer. Serve with zingy mustard or horseradish. Smacznego.

I took this to an office party and it disappeared. I found this recipe after looking for something easy because I had a class the night before the party. My version for a double batch: 1/2 c. everything (less sugar than suggested) and two 1 lb. packages (sliced thin on the diagonal) of kielbasa. Baked in the oven, as others suggested, for 90 minutes, stirring every 30 minutes. Super easy, super tasty, and not too expensive for a group. This will go into regular rotation. THANK YOU for sharing!

I followed the suggestions of other reviewers and doubled the sauce. I also added some onions and fried the onions and sausage for a few minutes before adding the sauce. I cooked it all on the stove with a lid for about 30 minutes since I don't have a slow cooker. I'll definitely make this again
Baked in oven. Sausage was great. Served with rice and broccoli. Added pineapple which made it very sweet. Might increase amount of horseradish next.
Added potatoes and bell peppers then baked it in the oven
Loved it and the family agrees that this would be awesome with baked beans and bacon.
I made this and baked also. I prefer the meat sliced thinner than what’s called for. It was very filling and delicious! Definitely adding this to the rotation!

My 10 year old picky eater loved it! I didn't have enough horseradish so I also threw in some dijon mustard and worcestershire sauce. I made it in the slow cooker but finished it off on the stovetop to thicken it up a bit. I will make again!

This is the best sauce I've found in a long time. I used beef kielbasa on the grill and in the air fryer, equally as delicious My seven year old grandson loved it. I may try it on rib eye steak. This is a keeper.
Love this recipe. So easy! Precooking the kielbasa a good way to reduce the grease. I also cut the sugar in half. Someone said it isn't a dinner recipe but I serve it with rice and broccoli. Delish!

Since there were only 2 of us I cut the recipe in 1/2 but then added 2 yams and also sliced then thin as the sausage. I couldn't see how the sauce would actually boil so I based the timing based on the yams cooking but not soft. It took a little over 2 hours and everything was terrific and there was a little left over but not for long.
I made this with vegan Kielbasa and it was surprisingly delicious. I don't like horseradish, so I substituted barbecue sauce and a dash of lemon juice. Very tasty!
